description: We are students from Trinity Preparatory School
summary: Last Signal is an interactive 3D educational open-world game that brings the stories of abandoned or inactive space equipment to life. As players walk around Mars and the Moon, exploring the environments, they learn more about how the equipment works, what its role was, what it accomplished, and the conditions it faced. Each piece of equipment also has an interactive activity to help the players understand it more. As players continuing exploring, they uncover the history of space exploration. Last signal provides a fun and interactive story-drive experience for people of all ages to learn about space exploration history. Players are sent to Mars or the Moon to preserve the knowledge contained in these pieces of equipment, and use what they learn to create their own rocket so they can fly back to Earth.
details:
How It Works

Players become explorers from Earth sent to investigate and learn from historical equipment on Mars and the Moon. After receiving the mission briefing, they select their destination and spacecraft before being transported there. After arriving, they explore different areas for equipment, and upon finishing an area, they can quick travel to the next area.

Each discovery introduces the equipment's purpose, mission history, operating conditions, accomplishments, and eventual fate. Players complete interactive activities that test their understanding of the underlying science and engineering. Successfully investigating equipment preserves historical knowledge in a personal mission archive.

The game currently includes 51 pieces of equipment, covering missions such as Apollo, Ingenuity, Perseverance, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, and InSight. Players can also explore the connections between discoveries and use their accumulated knowledge to unlock fictional spacecraft research systems, which they will use in the creation of a spacecraft to return back to Earth.

Scientific and Educational Value

Last Signal uses authentic NASA mission records, photographs, spacecraft models, and scientific datasets to connect exploration with real evidence.

Through descriptions and activities for each equipment, players can learn all about the science and history behind the equipment, teaching them about space exploration. For example, when players discover Ingenuity, they learn things like how atmospheric density affects helicopter lift on Mars through our interactive activity and text.

The Moon offers additional opportunities to learn about the equipment and hardware that was used in our history when exploring it; it also contains interactive activities and text

Technology and Development

Last Signal is a browser-based 3D game using TypeScript, React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and the Rapier physics engine. We used Blender for 3D modeling and rendering, Python and scientific computing libraries for processing planetary datasets, and Vite for development and production builds.

To accelerate our development, we used LLM's like ChatGPT and Claude.

Creativity and Design

Instead of presenting abandoned equipment as static museum exhibits, Last Signal turns historical research into an interactive story.

Players discover the equipment, investigate it, and preserve knowledge from it. This fictional expedition narrative provides a connection between separate missions while maintaining the distinctions those missions.

We focused on making the environments immersive without sacrificing scientific credibility. To create the assets, we used AI to generate them based off of real-life versions of the equipment and environment.

Intended Impact

Last Signal aims to make space exploration history and planetary science more engaging and accessible, especially for students and people who may not normally explore technical mission archives.

By combining exploration, storytelling, and scientific investigation, we hope to help players understand not only what these machines accomplished, but also the engineering challenges they overcame and the knowledge they left behind.

Our goal is to educate people about the history of space exploration in a way that is both fun and memorable.
